environment.network: Local production preview; no network or CPU throttling

adapters.limr: AsyncReader; default blocking Worker, default modules/TOC/sidebar/animations, automatic DOM windows
adapters.react-markdown: ReactMarkdown + remark-gfm + remark-math + rehype-katex + async Shiki; full DOM
adapters.markstream: MarkdownRender content + final=true; default virtualization/batching/lazy rendering/effects; package CSS, KaTeX and stream-diffs

measurement: Same complete UTF-8 corpus for every renderer, three fresh browser processes per case, production builds and default rich features. File acquisition as Blob is outside timing; decode, parse, rendering, font readiness and two rAFs precede first readable heading + paragraph. This is an application integration comparison, not identical parser or DOM work. LiMR uses its documented Worker/AsyncReader API; peers use their documented React APIs and have no added custom worker/windowing layer. Native scrolling checks peers; LiMR public source navigation checks its compressed scroll range. No forced GC. RSS sampled every 25ms, peak includes read probes; loading peak and idle memory are separate. Memory/time guards are symmetric and failed/incomplete content is retained, never ranked as successful fast rendering.
